items.t: LG AI연구원, ‘K-엑사원 2.5’ API 무료 공개…누구나 사용 가능
items.d: LG AI연구원이 9일 인공지능(AI) 모델 ‘K-엑사원 2.5’를 누구나 자신이 개발하는 서비스에 연결해 쓸 수 있도록 했다. 연구원 홈페이지에서 인증키를 발급받으면 응용프로그램 인터페이스(API)를 통해 이 모델을 무료로 쓸 수 있다.연구원은 이날 서울 강남구 코엑스에서 열린 ‘엔비디아 AI 데이 서울 2026’에서 K-엑사원 2.5를 선보였다. 이 모델은 연구원이 독자 AI 파운데이션 모델 개발 사업(독파모)을 통해 8월에 공개한 2차 모델의 성능을 끌어올려 만들었다. 개발자와 기업은 이렇게 개선한 모델을 각자 개발 중인 서비스에 연결해 실제 업무를 얼마나 잘 처리하는지 확인할 수 있다.연구원이 24개 지표로 자체 평가한 결과, 새 모델의 종합 성능은 8주 전 공개한 2차 모델보다 70% 이상 향상됐다

items.t: 젠슨 황 스캔들, K반도체에도 악재…공들인 ‘깐부’ 거취에 촉각
items.d: 젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)가 미국 정보당국이 중국 국가안전부 포섭 인물로 판단한 앨리스 황 전 메가스피드 임원과의 부적절한 관계를 인정했다. 엔비디아 이사회가 해당 의혹에 대한 조사를 시작하면서 향후 황 CEO의 경영권이 흔들릴 수 있을지에 관심이 쏠린다. 엔비디아에 경영 공백이 발생할 경우 협력 관계인 국내 기업에도 영향을 미칠 수 있다.8일(현지 시간) 엔비디아 이사회는 외부 법률 전문가가 참여하는 독립위원회를 구성해 황 CEO를 겨냥한 중국의 첩보 활동 의혹을 조사하겠다고 발표했다. 이사회의 조사 결과에 따라 황 CEO의 거취가 결정될 전망이다. 전 세계가 황 CEO의 스캔들을 주목하는 이유는 엔비디아가 현재 미국 증시를 이끌고 있는 거대 기업인 동시에, 최근 AI 기업들의 핵심 ‘자금줄’로

items.t: 엔비디아·SKT·리벨리온 손잡았다…국산 AI 반도체 해외 진출 모색
items.d: 국산 인공지능(AI) 반도체를 엔비디아의 그래픽처리장치(GPU)와 하나의 시스템에서 함께 사용하는 길이 열린다. 국내 AI 반도체 기업이 엔비디아의 기술을 기반으로 글로벌 데이터센터 시장에 진출할 발판을 마련할지 주목된다.9일 과학기술정보통신부에 따르면  이날 서울 코엑스에서 SK텔레콤과 국내 AI 반도체 기업 리벨리온은 엔비디아와 ‘NV링크 퓨전(NVLink Fusion)’ 협력을 위한 양해각서(MOU)를 체결했다. SK텔레콤이 조성하는 AI 데이터센터에 엔비디아 GPU와 리벨리온의 차세대 신경망처리장치(NPU) ‘리벨 R200’을 결합한 시스템을 도입하기 위한 기술 협력을 추진한다.NV링크 퓨전은 엔비디아의 고속 반도체 연결 기술을 바탕으로 외부 기업의 AI 반도체를 자사 시스템에 결합할 수 있도록 지원

Is Jensen Huang’s job on the line? Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates it’s “about a 50-50”
items.d: Nvidia’s board is investigating Jensen Huang over his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld thinks it’s roughly a coin flip whether Huang stays on as CEO.
items.fullText: Nvidia’s board announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang told staff he was unfaithful to his wife. But this isn’t a case of just another CEO having an extramarital affair. The romantic interest is Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy who was feeding information back to Beijing. In short, the stakes reach well beyond Nvidia, given how many tech and financial partners depend on its place at the center of the booming AI economy. “I’m responsible for an entire industry ,” Huang recently told Bloomberg in a sit-down. A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington dismissed the allegations in late October as “ groundless smears and slanders ,” and no one has been charged. But U.S. intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Donald Trump about their concerns a year ago, and unnamed senior officials inside the Trump administration told the Times that they doubt Huang could have remained unaware all that time of Alice Huang’s intelligence-gathering role for China. When Trump was first briefed, the Times reported, officials didn’t believe Huang knew, and isn’t clear whether their assessment has changed. The board, meanwhile, says it sees no sign that national security or company secrets were compromised. The question now is whether Huang can survive this. To think through what could come next, this editor spoke Sunday with famed professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management and founder of the Chief Executive Leadership Institute, which has hosted Huang at its CEO summits. Sonnenfeld likes Huang, he said, and he called Huang’s career salvageable but put the odds at “about a 50-50.” He also had a lot more food for thought. First, the damage. How Nvidia CEO’s Affair Engulfed AI Giant in Spy Probe
items.d: Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has admitted he had an affair. The woman was identified in a series of reports as a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chip colossus into a crisis like none before in its three-decade history. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: Nvidia CEO’s Affair Admission Counters Past Statements on Ties
items.d: For more than a year, Nvidia Corp. minimized the ties that Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang had with Megaspeed, the once-obscure spinoff of a Chinese gaming enterprise, and a woman named Huang Le who helped set it up.

items.fullText: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA November 8, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Tapping into the country’s strengths in manufacturing and engineering, NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem. The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles. These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production. Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering. In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST . Samsung is also exploring NVIDIA cuEquivariance to speed up tensor operations used in training and inference for atomistic AI models. Samsung is developing chip-scale thermal and mechanical analysis workflows with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo . In one AI homogenization case, combining AI-predicted effective material properties, coarser grids and GPU acceleration resulted in a roughly 1,600x speedup. Simulation time fell from about 18 hours for a fine-grid solve on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds for a GPU-accelerated coarse-grid solve. Looking ahead, NVIDIA Agent Toolkit could connect these simulation tools and AI models, helping future engineering agents run analyses and compare design options. items.fullText: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA Hyundai Motor Group and AIM Intelligence explore NVIDIA NemoClaw and OpenShell for secure enterprise agents, and LG AI Research opens API for ‘K-EXAONE-2.5’ trained on Nemotron datasets. November 8, 2026 by Nicola Sessions 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them. Hyundai Motor Group is exploring NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and the NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence is integrating its Starfort platform with NVIDIA OpenShell to support secure AI agents for employee productivity and enterprise workflows . A key component of the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, OpenShell provides a secure runtime with sandboxed execution and policy-based controls to safeguard sensitive data, manage access to enterprise tools and govern autonomous agent actions. AIM Intelligence , a Korean AI security company, is integrating its Starfort agent control platform with NVIDIA OpenShell. The goal is to combine OpenShell’s runtime access controls with Starfort’s detection of malicious instructions and data leakage. The company is also considering a preliminary proof of concept for the public energy sector, with potential applications across enterprise, industrial and robotics environments. On the model side, LG AI Research is opening application programming interface access for K-EXAONE-2.5, developed using NVIDIA Nemotron datasets, including Nemotron-Personas-Korea . Nemotron-Personas-Korea is an open dataset of 7 million fully synthetic Korean personas, grounded in official Korean statistics, that model builders use to ground training data and evaluation in Korean contexts. NVIDIA Nemotron is a family of open models, datasets and techniques that help developers build specialized, efficient AI agents. items.fullText: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration November 8, 2026 by Jesse Clayton 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security. The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization. Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference. In addition, NVIDIA today announced a collaboration with SK Telecom and Rebellions, supported by MSIT, to advance sovereign AI infrastructure for Korean models and workloads with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion. items.fullText: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production November 8, 2026 by Amr Elmeleegy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom , K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research , Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies . As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance. NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance. Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box. They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services. Learn more about NVIDIA Dynamo .
